about: Every study-record field the site reads, as paths into one record of data/demographics.partN.json.gz.

A path is a key ('status'), a key inside an object ('race.reported'), or a key on every item of a list ('study_sites[].country'). The contract asks that the key be present; its value may be null or empty, which is how a record says 'none'.

Classes say what reads the field. core: the dashboard, its filters (including the population filter's age fallback) and share links, over every record at load. studies_tab: the Studies table, its tooltips and the publications and breakdown views. detail: the study and geography-breakdown pop-ups only (status and why_stopped included: the table does not show them). A field read in more than one place takes the earliest class.

Where the classes live is the layout section below. A dataset whose core part 1 carries no layout key is inline: every class is on the records of data/demographics.partN.json.gz, as in every file published before the split and every existing snapshot. A split dataset keeps core in the parts and studies_tab and detail in their own files, which app.js fetches when the Studies tab or a pop-up needs them.

optional lists paths the site reads when a record carries them but that the records need not carry: a fallback chain such as a publication's title before its citation, official_title when brief_title is empty, or a raw category's omb_category before its category. The parts need not have them; a projection that keeps the listed fields keeps these too when they appear.

item_names maps a list, by its full path, to the variable names app.js uses for its items (study.references.map(ref => ...), rawCategories.filter(rc => ...)). Every member read through one of those names must be listed, as a class path or optional, on every list that name serves: one variable read across race, ethnicity, sex and gender items needs each field it reads on all four.

The engine reads this file and data_budget.json: its weekly publish refuses to push files that drop a listed field, and its split may write the layout section's files only while layout.enabled is true. tests/study_record_contract.test.mjs keeps the contract honest against app.js and checks the published files against it, inline or split.

not_record_fields._isAI: computed in app.js (isAIStudy) and cached on the record
not_record_fields.reference_count: carried only by dashboard-summary.json recentStudies rows (mobile and archives); a fallback when references is absent

about: How a dataset's study records are laid out in files: the one spec the engine's split (scripts/split_data.py), its publish gate (scripts/check_site_contract.py) and app.js's reader all follow. Version 1.

enabled is the owner's switch. The engine writes split files only while the live site contract has version 1 and enabled true; otherwise it publishes whole-record parts (inline). The reader reads both either way, so turning the split on, or off again, is a one-line site change.

A dataset is one folder: data/ for the latest run, snapshots/<date>/ for an archived week, each with its own files. Core part 1's header says how its records are laid out. No layout key: inline, every class on the records. A layout object, {"version": 1, "studies_tab": {"files": total_parts}, "detail": {"shards": N, "key": "nct_number_mod"}}, identical in every core part: split. app.js refuses a dataset whose parts disagree about it, whose studies_tab.files is not total_parts, or whose version or key it does not know ("this page is older than the data; reload").

files gives each class's file names. {K} is 1..total_parts. A studies_tab part K holds exactly core part K's studies. {n} is 0..shards-1, unpadded: a study's detail is in shard n = Number(nct_id.slice(3)) % shards (detail.key nct_number_mod; vectors lists the test vectors both repositories check), every core study exactly once.

headers lists the keys each file carries. data is the core records as a list, in order; in a studies_tab part or a detail shard it is an object keyed by nct_id. Every file of a dataset carries its run stamps, extracted_at and pipeline_commit, equal to core part 1's; the reader fetches a file with other stamps once more past the browser cache, and if it still differs uses nothing from it.

Each class file carries its class's paths plus the optional paths optional_class assigns to it (an optional path rides with the class whose path shares its container). Paths in no class and not optional are dropped. whole_lists are written whole in the detail shards, so the shard's list replaces the core's (study_sites in core carries country only).

archive is an aggregate (summary-only) archive's own file of study records: the full projection of every class and optional path for exactly its summary's recentStudies, keyed by nct_id, stamped with the run it was projected from (source_pipeline_commit may be null when that run's parts carried none). history.json names it, "archives": {"<date>": {"kind": "aggregate", "detail": "archive_records.json.gz"}}, with dates kept a list of strings for older pages. Until an archive has one, 2026-02-22 (extracted before 2026-03-05) reads the frozen data/details files, labelled as that extract, and every other aggregate says "Not included in this archive".
